evals.prompt: Generate an interactive UML diagram of the architecture of the repo at /Users/jackzhang/khan/youtube-pipelines. I want a high-level view of the whole system first, with the ability to drill down into the details of each pipeline. Make it a single HTML file I can open in my browser.
evals.expected_output: A self-contained interactive HTML architecture diagram with a small high-level view (actors, pipelines, external systems like YouTube API), drill-down into the captions/videos pipelines, labeled edges, and detail sidebars grounded in real file paths.
assertions: Deliverable is a single HTML file that renders in a headless browser with no error banner and no uncaught JS console errors
HTML is fully self-contained: no <script src> or <link href> pointing at external http(s) hosts (works offline)
Top-level view is a readable abstraction: between 3 and 11 components, not one box per file
Drill-down works: at least one top-level component expands into a deeper level of detail
Connections between components are labeled with descriptive interaction text (not bare arrows)
Component details are grounded in the real repo: clicking/inspecting components surfaces file paths that actually exist under /Users/jackzhang/khan/youtube-pipelines
Architecture matches reality: both the captions pipeline and the videos pipeline appear as distinct components, and YouTube (API) appears as an external system
At least one sequence-diagram-style flow of a key scenario is included
Sync vs async/data interactions are visually distinguished (different arrow/line styles with a legend or equivalent)
